newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Red Cross delays food shipment to North.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Red Cross delays food shipment to North.

text.p: The South Korean Red Cross delayed sending food aid to North Korea because of a shipping problem, the Unification Ministry said on Saturday.
The aid is the first since a North Korean submarine incursion in September, which prompted South Korea to freeze all contacts with the communist country.
"The shipment, originally scheduled for today, will be made around January 31," said a ministry spokesman.
He said the ship which was to carry 300 tonnes of flour and 15,000 pairs of socks failed to load the cargo due to a delay in unloading a previous consignment.
The flour and socks bought from donations by religious groups in the country is worth $153,000.

On Friday, the world Red Cross body IFRC issued an urgent appeal for support for its aid programme to flood-hit North Korea, where persistent reports say tens of thousands of people are on starvation rations.

"The situation is critical," said a statement from the IFRC, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies which has been working in the country for two years to bring relief to some of the worst-hit areas.

Seoul has gradually eased restrictions on contacts with North Korea after Pyongyang issued a rare apology last month for sending a submarine that dropped 26 intruders on a Southern beach last September.
Shortly after the apology, Seoul returned the remains of 24 of the infiltrators who were shot dead. One was captured alive and the other is still at large.
South Korea opened the door for local companies to do business in North Korea on Friday for the first time since the submarine incident.
The ministry said it gave approval to seven domestic companies to contact North Koreans for business ranging from garment-making to soft drinks.
